name: Amie
tagline: Combine calendar, tasks, contacts, and scheduling in a polished daily interface
verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Amie, combine calendar, tasks, contacts, and scheduling in a polished daily interface. The hard boundary is native polish, sync, calendar providers, mobile apps, and integrated communications, plus calendar integrations and reliability.
coreLoopDIY: Read one calendar, combine tasks and contacts in a daily view, publish availability, create conflict-safe bookings, and send confirmations and reminders.
whatYouLose: native polish, sync, calendar providers, mobile apps, and integrated communications
ongoingBurden: OAuth refresh, webhooks, timezone databases, race conditions, reminders, deliverability, privacy, and uptime
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Amie because people pay because one double booking or missed invite can cost more than years of subscription fees. The recurring cost buys OAuth refresh, webhooks, timezone databases, race conditions, reminders, deliverability, privacy, and uptime, not just the visible interface.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Morgen
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Everyone recommends it; in 2026 it is a 14-day trial followed by a subscription.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Notion Calendar
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Good calendar-and-task shell, but it has no contact layer and therefore does not replace Amie’s actual bundle.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Routine Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The free plan lacks time blocking and still has no real contacts layer; the attractive daily-planner part starts paid.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a single-user booking service DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Amie in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, Google Calendar OAuth, and Resend; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: read one calendar, combine tasks and contacts in a daily view, publish availability, create conflict-safe bookings, and send confirmations and reminders.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement one account with configurable working hours, buffers, minimum notice, and booking horizon.
Connect Google Calendar using OAuth and store refresh tokens encrypted at rest.
Calculate availability in UTC and render it in the visitor's detected timezone.
Reserve slots transactionally, create calendar events, and prevent concurrent double booking.
Send confirmation, cancellation, and reminder email with signed management links.
Add an admin booking list, event-type editor, audit log, and calendar reconnect flow.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out Microsoft and Apple calendar support.
Deliberately leave out team round-robin routing.
Deliberately leave out payments, CRM workflows, and enterprise controls.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
